questions.question: Who has the authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies is vested in the **Parliament of India**.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies are governed by the **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002**, which was enacted by Parliament.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies operate in more than one state, and hence, come under the purview of the **Union List** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 246 of the Constitution assigns legislative powers over subjects in the Union List exclusively to Parliament.
 
• The Department of Co-operation, under the Ministry of Co-operation, oversees the implementation and regulation of laws concerning multi-state co-operative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002:**

 
 
• It regulates the functioning of co-operative societies that operate across multiple states in India.
 
• The Act emphasizes democratic management, accountability, and transparency in co-operative societies.
 
• It provides provisions for registration, management, and dissolution of multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Union List:**
 
 
• The Union List is one of the three lists under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains subjects on which only Parliament has the exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Co-operation:**
 
 
• Established in July 2021 to promote and strengthen co-operative societies across India.
 
• Its responsibilities include formulating policies and implementing programs related to co-operatives.
 
• The ministry also aims to streamline processes for multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Article 246 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Defines the distribution of legislative powers between Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• Subjects listed under the Union List are exclusively under Parliament’s jurisdiction.
 
• Co-operative societies operating across multiple states fall under Parliament's legislative domain due to their inclusion in the Union List.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT allowed under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dual citizenship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955 governs the acquisition, determination, and termination of Indian citizenship.
 
• India does not allow **dual citizenship**. A citizen of India cannot hold citizenship of another country simultaneously.
 
• The Act provides for citizenship through five modes: **birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory**.
 
• Dual citizenship is not permitted because India follows a policy of single citizenship, ensuring uniform national identity and allegiance.
 
• Indian citizens acquiring foreign citizenship must renounce their Indian citizenship as per the provisions of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naturalization:**

 
 
• Naturalization is a mode of acquiring citizenship for foreign nationals who fulfill eligibility criteria like residence in India for a specified period and good character.
 
• Applicants must renounce their citizenship of another country to become Indian citizens.
 
 
 
• **Descent-based Citizenship:**
 
 
• A person born outside India is considered an Indian citizen by descent if either of their parents is an Indian citizen.
 
• Specific conditions apply based on the date of birth and registration requirements under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
 
 
• **Registration:**
 
 
• Citizenship through registration is available for individuals like persons of Indian origin or spouses of Indian citizens who meet prescribed conditions.
 
• They must reside in India for a specific period before applying for registration.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI):**
 
 
• Though dual citizenship is not allowed, the government offers the **OCI scheme** for people of Indian origin who are citizens of other countries.
 
• OCI status provides several rights but does not equate to full citizenship, such as voting rights or eligibility for government jobs.
 
 
 
• **Renunciation and Termination of Citizenship:**
 
 
• Citizenship can be renounced voluntarily by individuals or terminated by the government in case of fraud or disloyalty.
 
• The Act specifies detailed procedures for renunciation and termination to ensure compliance with legal frameworks.

questions.question: Following the provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992, which of the following terms is used for urban governance in areas transitioning from rural to urban?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagar Panchayats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• es Nagar Panchayats are urban local bodiestablished under the provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
 
• They are constituted for areas transitioning from rural to urban due to population growth or other factors of urbanization.
 
• The primary purpose of Nagar Panchayats is to manage urban governance in these transitional areas while ensuring smooth administrative operations.
 
• As per the Constitution, Nagar Panchayats are recognized as one of the three types of municipal entities: Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, and Nagar Panchayats.
 
• Nagar Panchayats consist of elected representatives and function under the control of the state government, addressing urban planning, development, and basic infrastructure needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**

 
 
• This amendment introduced the concept of urban local bodies, including Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, and Nagar Panchayats.
 
• It provided constitutional recognition to local governance and decentralized decision-making in urban areas.
 
• The act aimed at empowering urban local bodies to function as institutions of self-government under Article 243Q.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in India**
 
 
• India's urban population is steadily growing due to migration, industrialization, and expansion of economic opportunities.
 
• Transitional areas often require structured urban governance to address challenges like housing, sanitation, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Nagar Panchayats and Rural Bodies**
 
 
• While rural bodies like Gram Panchayats cater to villages, Nagar Panchayats focus on urban governance in transitioning areas.
 
• Nagar Panchayats deal with urban challenges such as traffic management, waste disposal, and urban planning.
 
 
 
• **Role of State Governments**
 
 
• State governments play a crucial role in defining the criteria for establishing Nagar Panchayats.
 
• They provide funds, guidance, and administrative support to enable effective urban governance.

questions.question: What major power did the 74th Amendment Act, 1992, provide to Urban Local Bodies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitutional outline for governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 74th Amendment Act, 1992, provided a **constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**, ensuring their governance framework under the Indian Constitution.
 
• The amendment added **Part IX-A** (The Municipalities) to the Constitution, detailing the structure, composition, and functions of ULBs.
 
• It mandated the creation of three types of municipalities: **Nagar Panchayats**, **Municipal Councils**, and **Municipal Corporations**, based on population size.
 
• It introduced the concept of **decentralized governance**, empowering ULBs to plan and implement development programs and manage local resources effectively.
 
• The act also provided for the establishment of a **State Finance Commission (SFC)** to allocate financial resources to these bodies, ensuring fiscal autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IX-A of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Introduced by the 74th Amendment, it provides a **constitutional framework for urban governance**.
 
• It includes Articles 243P to 243ZG, outlining the composition, powers, and responsibilities of municipalities.
 
 
 
• **State Finance Commission (SFC):**
 
 
• Established under Article 243-I, it ensures **equitable distribution of financial resources** between the state government and ULBs.
 
• The SFC reviews financial positions of ULBs and recommends measures for their fiscal sustainability.
 
 
 
• **District Planning Committees (DPCs):**
 
 
• Mandated under Article 243ZD, DPCs integrate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities into a cohesive **district development plan**.
 
 
 
• **Empowered Municipalities:**
 
 
• The 12th Schedule of the Constitution lists **18 functional areas** for ULBs, including urban planning, water supply, sanitation, and public health.
 
• This ensures enhanced autonomy and accountability in addressing local governance issues.

questions.question: When appointing judges to the High Courts, the President of India is required to consult which officials apart from the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of the respective State?

options.text: The members of the State Legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The State Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 217 of the Indian Constitution, the President is required to consult the Chief Justice of India, the Chief Justice of the respective High Court, and the **Governor of the concerned State** before appointing judges to the High Courts.
 
• The role of the State Governor in this process is advisory, and the final decision is made by the President.
 
• The consultation process ensures the appointment of qualified and unbiased individuals to the judiciary, maintaining the integrity of the judicial system.
 
• The Chief Justice of India plays a critical role in providing recommendations to the President based on merit and judicial expertise.
 
• This constitutional provision is designed to promote a collaborative process involving key stakeholders in the judiciary and executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 217 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• It deals with the appointment and conditions of service of High Court judges.
 
• The President appoints judges after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the concerned state, and sometimes other judges as deemed necessary.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of India provides recommendations to the President, ensuring judicial appointments are based on merit and integrity.
 
• This role is crucial for maintaining the independence of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **High Court Judges:**
 
 
• They are responsible for adjudicating cases and upholding the Constitution within their respective jurisdictions.
 
• High Court judges hold office until the age of 62.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Advisory Role:**
 
 
• The Governor of the state provides input during the consultation process, representing the state’s interests.
 
• While the Governor’s role is advisory, the President has the final say in judicial appointments.

questions.question: In India, judicial review is considered as:

options.text: The power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the executive orders after they are passed by the Union cabinet
the power of the judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the legislatures

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Judicial review in India is a power granted to the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders.
 
• This principle ensures that laws and executive actions do not violate the provisions of the Constitution of India.
 
• The concept is derived from Article 13, which states that any law inconsistent with the Constitution shall be void.
 
• Judicial review in India encompasses reviewing administrative decisions, legislative enactments, and constitutional amendments.
 
• It acts as a crucial mechanism for maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution and protecting fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• Judicial review originated in the United States through the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**.
 
• It ensures checks and balances among the three organs of the government: executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• In India, judicial review is limited compared to the United States but is pivotal in safeguarding constitutional democracy.
 
 
 
• **Articles Related to Judicial Review in India**
 
 
• **Article 13:** Declares that laws inconsistent with or in derogation of fundamental rights are void.
 
• **Article 32:** Provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing citizens to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of rights.
 
• **Article 226:** Empowers High Courts to issue orders or writs for enforcement of fundamental rights and other purposes.
 
 
 
• **Types of Judicial Review**
 
 
• **Review of Legislative Actions:** Ensures that laws passed by the legislature adhere to constitutional provisions.
 
• **Review of Executive Actions:** Examines the validity of decisions made by the executive branch.
 
• **Review of Constitutional Amendments:** Determines whether amendments violate the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine**
 
 
• This doctrine was established in the landmark **Keshavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
• The judiciary can strike down constitutional amendments if they violate the essential features of the Constitution.
 
• Examples of basic structure elements include the supremacy of the Constitution, secularism, and judicial independence.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment recognised the right to form cooperative societies as a part of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**97th Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 recognized the **right to form cooperative societies** as a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added a new Directive Principle of State Policy under **Article 43B**, which directs the state to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, and democratic control of cooperative societies.
 
• The Amendment introduced Part IXB to the Constitution, which deals specifically with the incorporation, regulation, and functioning of cooperative societies.
 
• The Act aimed to ensure the independence and democratic functioning of cooperatives, enhance their accountability, and improve their governance structure.
 
• It empowered citizens to form and operate cooperative societies without undue state interference, thereby strengthening grassroots-level economic democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 19(1)(c):** This article guarantees all citizens the right to form associations or unions, which now includes cooperative societies after the 97th Amendment.
 
• **Article 43B:** Added through the 97th Amendment, it directs the state to promote cooperative societies as an important tool for socio-economic development.
 
• **Part IXB:** This part of the Constitution specifically governs the structure, composition, elections, and auditing of cooperative societies across the country.
 
• **Cooperative Societies:** These are voluntary associations of individuals who come together for a common economic objective, such as agriculture, credit, or housing.
 
• **Supreme Court Judgment:** In 2021, the Supreme Court struck down the application of Part IXB to multi-state cooperative societies but upheld its validity for state cooperatives, maintaining federal balance.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution promotes the spread and development of Hindi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 351**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 351** of the Indian Constitution is specifically aimed at promoting the spread and development of the Hindi language.
 
• It directs the Union Government to promote Hindi so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all elements of the composite culture of India.
 
• The article also highlights the importance of assimilating forms, styles, and expressions from other Indian languages to enrich Hindi.
 
• It aims to make Hindi the lingua franca while respecting linguistic diversity and ensuring inclusivity in India’s cultural and linguistic heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Constitution and Language:**

 
 
• Part XVII of the Constitution deals with the official language of the Republic of India.
 
• Articles 343 to 351 specifically focus on language-related provisions.
 
 
 
• **Article 343:**
 
 
• Declares Hindi in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union.
 
• English was permitted to be used for official purposes for an initial period of 15 years after the Constitution came into effect.
 
 
 
• **Article 350:**
 
 
• Allows individuals to submit representations for the redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or the state.
 
 
 
• **Efforts to Promote Hindi:**
 
 
• Institutions such as Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Central Hindi Directorate work to implement the provisions of Article 351.
 
• Various schemes and awards are introduced by the government to promote the use of Hindi.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the three levels/tiers in the Panchayati Raj system in India?

options.text: Gram Sabha, Municipal Council, Cantonment Board
Gram Panchayat, Block Assemblies, State Assembly
Village Panchayat, Municipal Corporation, Zilla Parishad
Village Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zilla Parishad

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Village Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zilla Parishad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Panchayati Raj system in India operates at three tiers: **Village Panchayat (Gram Panchayat), Block Samiti (Intermediate Panchayat), and Zilla Parishad (District Panchayat).**
 
• **Village Panchayat**: The lowest level of the Panchayati Raj system, responsible for local governance at the village level.
 
• **Block Samiti**: The intermediate level, governing a group of villages within a block or tehsil.
 
• **Zilla Parishad**: The highest tier, responsible for governance at the district level, overseeing multiple blocks.
 
• This structure was institutionalized under the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gram Sabha**: It is the general assembly comprising all registered voters in a village. It serves as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system, but it is not considered a tier.
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act**: Passed in 1992, it introduced Part IX in the Constitution, providing constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and mandating their formation in every state.
 
• **State Election Commission**: Responsible for conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions, ensuring free and fair electoral processes.
 
• **Functions of Panchayati Raj Institutions**: Include rural development, sanitation, public health, maintenance of water resources, and agricultural development.
 
• **Article 243**: Defines the provisions for Panchayati Raj, including Gram Sabha's role, composition, powers, and functions of Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.question: Under Article 164(3) of the Constitution of India, who administers the oath of office to the State Ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 164(3) of the Constitution of India, the **Governor of the State administers the oath of office** and secrecy to the State Ministers.
 
• The oath is administered in accordance with the **form prescribed in the Third Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor acts as the **constitutional head of the state** and performs this function as part of their responsibilities.
 
• The oath ceremony typically takes place in the presence of other dignitaries, and the **Chief Minister recommends the names of the ministers** to the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 164 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• It outlines the appointment and tenure of the Chief Minister and other ministers in a state.
 
• The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and on the advice of the Chief Minister, appoints other ministers.
 
 
 
• **Third Schedule of the Constitution:**
 
 
• It contains the forms of oath or affirmation for various constitutional posts, including ministers.
 
• The oath emphasizes the duty to uphold the Constitution and work without fear or favor.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor is the **nominal executive head** of the state, while the real executive powers lie with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• As per the Constitution, the Governor administers oaths, summons the legislature, and ensures the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker presides over the sessions of the legislative assembly but does not administer oaths to ministers.
 
• The Speaker's role is primarily related to legislative procedures, debates, and maintaining order in the house.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• The Constitution ensures a clear distinction between the roles of the executive, legislature, and judiciary to maintain a balance of power.
 
• The Governor's role as the administrator of oaths is part of the executive function.

questions.question: The Indian High Courts Act was passed in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1861**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian High Courts Act was passed in **1861** during British rule in India.
 
• This act paved the way for the establishment of **High Courts in major presidencies** such as Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
• It replaced the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats that were functioning in these presidencies at the time.
 
• The High Courts established under this act were vested with **civil, criminal, and appellate jurisdiction**.
 
• The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 is considered a significant step in the judicial reforms in colonial India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats:**

 
 
• Before the High Courts were established, **Supreme Courts** functioned in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
• **Sadar Adalats** were the principal courts of appeal in civil and criminal cases in the provinces.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms under British Rule:**
 
 
• The British introduced several judicial reforms to consolidate their administrative control over India.
 
• The Indian High Courts Act was part of these reforms aimed at improving the efficiency and structure of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Indian High Courts Act of 1861:**
 
 
• It allowed the Crown to establish High Courts by Letters Patent in the presidencies.
 
• The High Courts were modeled on the British judicial system, ensuring uniformity and better administration of justice.
 
 
 
• **Modern Relevance:**
 
 
• High Courts continue to function as the principal civil and criminal courts of appeal in India.
 
• The judiciary in India still follows the hierarchical structure introduced during British rule.

questions.question: How many functional items are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution for Panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains **29 functional items** that specify the responsibilities of Panchayats.
 
• These items were added by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**, which came into effect on **24 April 1993**.
 
• The schedule focuses on empowering Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to function as units of self-government.
 
• Functional items include areas such as agriculture, rural development, education, health, sanitation, and public distribution systems.
 
• The inclusion of these items aims to decentralize governance and promote community participation in local administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• Passed in 1992, it provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
 
• Introduced Part IX in the Constitution and added Articles 243 to 243(O).
 
• Mandated the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zilla Parishad.
 
 
 
• **Key Functional Areas in the Eleventh Schedule:**
 
 
• Rural housing, drinking water, roads, and irrigation.
 
• Animal husbandry, fisheries, and minor forest produce.
 
• Non-conventional energy sources, adult education, and public health.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Decentralization:**
 
 
• Enhances grassroots democracy and local self-governance.
 
• Empowers rural communities to participate in decision-making processes.
 
• Promotes accountability, transparency, and efficiency in governance.
 
 
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:**
 
 
• Recommended the establishment of Panchayati Raj Institutions in 1957.
 
• Advocated for democratic decentralization to strengthen local governance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the Indian Union Cabinet’s role in legislation?

options.text: The Cabinet is the only law-making body in India.
The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.
The Cabinet enacts laws without any involvement of any house of the Indian Parliament.
The Cabinet has judicial authority over legislations surpassing the judiciary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Union Cabinet plays a key role in the legislative process by **formulating and finalizing government bills** before they are introduced in Parliament.
 
• It is responsible for **preparing the legislative agenda**, which outlines the government’s priority bills to be discussed in Parliament.
 
• The Cabinet ensures that proposed legislations align with **government policies and objectives**.
 
• After the Cabinet approves a bill, it is introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha for deliberation and eventual enactment.
 
• The Cabinet does not have the authority to enact laws directly; it acts as an **executive body** within the structure of parliamentary democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Cabinet**:

 
 
• The Union Cabinet is a part of the Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is responsible for the formulation of policies and implementation of laws in India.
 
• The Cabinet operates under the framework of the Indian Constitution, which establishes the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process in India**:
 
 
• Legislation in India involves drafting bills, deliberation in Parliament, and Presidential assent.
 
• The government primarily introduces bills that reflect its policies and priorities.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliament**:
 
 
• Both the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) deliberate on bills to ensure comprehensive scrutiny.
 
• The Parliament enacts laws, while the Cabinet facilitates the process by preparing and proposing bills.
 
 
 
• **Checks and Balances**:
 
 
• The Cabinet cannot bypass the legislative authority of Parliament.
 
• This ensures a balance of power between the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government.

questions.question: How many times may the President of India ask the Prime Minister to have an executive recommendation reconsidered by the Cabinet?

options.text: It is at the President's absolute discretion without limits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only once**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India has the constitutional authority to return an executive recommendation to the Prime Minister for reconsideration by the Cabinet, but this can only be done **once**.
 
• This authority is granted under **Article 78** of the Indian Constitution, which outlines the duties of the Prime Minister in advising the President.
 
• If the Cabinet reaffirms its decision after reconsideration, the President is bound to accept the recommendation and act accordingly.
 
• This constitutional mechanism ensures a balance between the executive's decision-making power and the President's oversight role.
 
• The provision highlights the President's role as a constitutional head, who must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 78 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• It defines the Prime Minister's duties concerning communication between the President and the Council of Ministers.
 
• It mandates the Prime Minister to keep the President informed of all decisions of the Cabinet related to the administration of India.
 
• The article ensures the President is aware of the governance and policy decisions while maintaining a ceremonial role.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Indian Parliamentary Democracy**
 
 
• The President is the constitutional head of state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President's role is largely ceremonial, with real executive power resting with the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Reconsideration Mechanism**
 
 
• The mechanism allows the President to return legislative and executive proposals for reconsideration.
 
• It is a tool to ensure thorough deliberation by the Cabinet, especially in cases of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Checks and Balances**
 
 
• India's parliamentary democracy incorporates checks and balances to prevent the misuse of power.
 
• The President's ability to seek reconsideration is an example of such a safeguard.

questions.question: Where can people of Indian origin living abroad apply for Indian citizenship under Article 8?

options.text: Indian Embassy at their country of living

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Embassy at their country of living**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 8 of the Constitution of India, persons of Indian origin residing outside the country can apply for Indian citizenship at the **Indian Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence**.
 
• Article 8 specifically provides for Indian citizenship to those who have Indian origin but are **ordinarily residing outside India**.
 
• The individual must be registered as a citizen of India by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in that country.
 
• The process involves verification of the applicant's Indian origin and other supporting documentation by the concerned diplomatic mission.
 
• This provision is part of the broader framework of the Indian Constitution's citizenship laws, which include Articles 5 to 11.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• These articles deal with the acquisition and termination of citizenship in India.
 
• They provide the constitutional framework for Indian citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution in 1950.
 
• Article 8 is particularly relevant for individuals of Indian origin living abroad.
 
 
 
• **Indian Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• This act governs the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship after the Constitution came into effect.
 
• It provides various modes for acquiring citizenship, such as birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI):**
 
 
• OCI is a scheme launched by the Government of India to facilitate individuals of Indian origin who do not qualify for Indian citizenship but want to maintain a connection with India.
 
• OCI does not grant full citizenship but provides certain privileges like visa-free travel and property ownership in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora:**
 
 
• The Indian diaspora is one of the largest in the world, with millions of individuals of Indian origin living in various countries.
 
• They play a significant role in fostering economic, cultural, and political ties between India and their countries of residence.

questions.question: What major tax reform was introduced by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the **101st Amendment Act, 2016**.
 
• It was implemented on **July 1, 2017**, replacing multiple indirect taxes like service tax, VAT, and excise duty.
 
• GST is a **destination-based tax**, meaning it is levied at the point of consumption rather than the point of origin.
 
• The tax structure includes four main slabs: **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**, depending on the type of goods and services.
 
• GST is governed by a dual structure, where both the Central Government (CGST) and State Governments (SGST) collect taxes on intra-state transactions, while inter-state transactions attract Integrated GST (IGST).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Input Tax Credit (ITC):**

 
 
• Under GST, businesses can claim credit for taxes paid on purchases as a set-off against taxes payable on sales.
 
• This eliminates the cascading effect of taxes, making the tax system more efficient.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
 
• It consists of representatives from both the Central and State Governments to decide GST rates, policies, and reforms.
 
 
 
• **Types of GST:**
 
 
• **CGST:** Central Goods and Services Tax, levied by the central government.
 
• **SGST:** State Goods and Services Tax, levied by state governments.
 
• **IGST:** Integrated Goods and Services Tax, applicable on inter-state transactions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GST:**
 
 
• GST has simplified the tax structure in India by consolidating multiple indirect taxes.
 
• It has improved tax compliance and brought transparency to the taxation system.
 
• It has boosted India's ease of doing business rankings by streamlining tax processes for businesses.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 specifically for children?

options.text: Right of children to free and compulsory education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right of children to free and compulsory education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002** inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This amendment guarantees **free and compulsory education** for children in the specified age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE Act) was enacted in **2009** to operationalize Article 21A.
 
• Under the RTE Act, schools are mandated to provide necessary infrastructure, trained teachers, and ensure non-discrimination.
 
• This right aims to enhance literacy rates, promote social equity, and empower children across all socio-economic backgrounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21A:** It states that "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years as determined by law."
 
• **RTE Act, 2009:** This legislation specifies the norms and standards for schools, prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment, and ensures inclusive education for disadvantaged groups.
 
• **Constitutional Significance:** The 86th Amendment also modified **Article 45** (Directive Principles of State Policy) to prioritize early childhood care and education for children below six years.
 
• **Global Context:** India's efforts align with the **United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**, advocating for universal access to education.
 
• **Impact:** The RTE Act and Article 21A have significantly contributed to improving enrollment rates and reducing dropouts, especially among marginalized communities.

questions.question: When appointing Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, the President of India acts on the advice of which body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Council of Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India appoints Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories based on the advice of the **Union Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This is in accordance with the principle of the parliamentary system, where the President acts on the advice of the executive body.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers is responsible for aiding and advising the President in exercising their constitutional powers.
 
• Article **74(1)** of the Indian Constitution mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Governors serve as the constitutional head of the state, and their appointment is a part of the President's discretionary powers, executed in consultation with the executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Council of Ministers:**

 
 
• The Union Council of Ministers comprises the Prime Minister and other ministers, including Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, as per Article 75 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state and ensures that the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• They are responsible for summoning and proroguing the state legislature, appointing the Chief Minister, and giving assent to state bills.
 
 
 
• **Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• The Lieutenant Governor is the administrative head of Union Territories like Delhi, Puducherry, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• They exercise powers delegated to them by the President of India under various provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 74 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• Mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
 
• This ensures that India follows the principles of a parliamentary democracy with a nominal head of state.

questions.question: The award (decision) made by the Lok Adalats is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and is final and binding on all parties because:

options.text: An appeal can be filed in the Supreme Court
A review petition can be filed
An appeal can be filed in the High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No appeal is permissible**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The award or decision of a Lok Adalat is deemed as equivalent to a decree of a civil court under the provisions of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• Once a settlement is reached in Lok Adalat, it is binding on all parties and no appeal is permissible to challenge the decision.
 
• Lok Adalat promotes voluntary conciliation and consensus-based dispute resolution, ensuring quicker and cost-effective justice.
 
• It is designed to avoid prolonged litigation by resolving disputes amicably without the need for a formal trial.
 
• The finality of the award is emphasized to maintain the efficiency and credibility of Lok Adalats as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat:**

 
 
• Lok Adalat (People's Court) is a statutory body under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• It is organized to provide free legal aid and resolve disputes through conciliation and compromise.
 
• Cases like civil disputes, matrimonial disputes, labor disputes, and compoundable criminal cases are usually resolved by Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:**
 
 
• This Act provides the framework for organizing Lok Adalats and ensuring free legal aid to economically weaker sections.
 
• It establishes State and District Legal Services Authorities to oversee the implementation of legal aid and Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Eliminates the lengthy process of litigation and provides speedy justice.
 
• Reduces the burden on regular courts and saves resources.
 
• Fosters mutual understanding and peace among disputing parties.
 
 
 
• **Binding Nature of Awards:**
 
 
• The award is final and cannot be appealed, ensuring quick and decisive resolution of disputes.
 
• Parties must voluntarily agree to the settlement before the award is passed.

questions.question: Which of the following documents are NOT required under CAA 2019 to apply for Indian citizenship?

__
 
• Under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019, applicants are not required to submit a **Birth Certificate** to apply for Indian citizenship.
 
• The CAA 2019 facilitates citizenship for persons belonging to Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, or Christian communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, or Pakistan who entered India before **December 31, 2014**.
 
• Documents like **Passport and Visa**, along with proof of religion and country of origin, are sufficient for processing applications under CAA 2019.
 
• Other documents like Aadhaar Card or Voter ID may be used as supplementary evidence but are not mandatory for citizenship application under CAA.
 
• The CAA does not apply to Muslims or undocumented individuals who entered India after the specified cutoff date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019:**

 
 
• It was passed in December 2019 to amend the Citizenship Act of 1955.
 
• The act grants fast-track citizenship to religious minorities facing persecution in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan.
 
• The primary beneficiaries are Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility under CAA:**
 
 
• Applicants must prove their entry into India before **December 31, 2014**.
 
• Documentary evidence showing persecution in their country of origin may be required.
 
• The cutoff date is strictly adhered to under the provisions of the act.
 
 
 
• **Criticism and Controversy:**
 
 
• The CAA has been criticized for excluding Muslim refugees and for being potentially discriminatory.
 
• It triggered protests and debates across India regarding its constitutionality and impact on secularism.
 
 
 
• **Proof of Citizenship:**
 
 
• Applicants may use various documents such as passports, voter ID cards, or other identity documents to substantiate their claims.
 
• The process is overseen by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.question: What is the Forty-Second Amendment of the Indian Constitution commonly known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mini-Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Forty-Second Amendment of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1976**, is commonly referred to as the **Mini-Constitution** due to its extensive and comprehensive nature.
 
• It was introduced during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** and is one of the most far-reaching amendments in the history of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The amendment affected **59 Articles** and added **14 new Articles**, significantly altering the Constitution's structure.
 
• It introduced the terms **"Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity"** in the Preamble, emphasizing the core values of the Indian state.
 
• The amendment also curtailed the power of the judiciary, strengthened the authority of Parliament, and redefined the relationship between the Executive and Judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emergency Period:** The amendment was passed during the Emergency (1975–1977), a period characterized by significant centralization of power and suppression of dissent.
 
• **Directive Principles:** It gave primacy to the Directive Principles of State Policy over Fundamental Rights, emphasizing the welfare state model.
 
• **Tenure of Lok Sabha and State Assemblies:** The amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from **5 to 6 years**.
 
• **Judicial Review:** It restricted the judiciary's ability to challenge constitutional amendments and curtailed its power to review laws passed by Parliament.
 
• **Criticism:** The Forty-Second Amendment faced widespread criticism for its authoritarian nature, and many of its provisions were later repealed or modified by the **Forty-Fourth Amendment Act (1978)**.

questions.question: Which landmark case first established the principle of judicial review in constitutional law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marbury v. Madison (1803)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Marbury v. Madison (1803)** was a landmark decision by the Supreme Court of the United States that established the principle of **judicial review**.
 
• Judicial review allows the judiciary to review and invalidate laws or executive actions that are deemed unconstitutional, ensuring adherence to the Constitution.
 
• This case was presided over by Chief Justice **John Marshall**, who emphasized the judiciary's role as an independent arbiter of the Constitution.
 
• The case arose when William Marbury petitioned the Supreme Court to compel delivery of his commission as justice of the peace, which was denied by the incoming administration.
 
• The decision clarified the balance of powers among the legislative, executive, and judicial branches, solidifying the judiciary's authority as equal to other branches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:**

 
 
• Judicial review is the power of courts to assess whether laws and executive actions are consistent with the Constitution.
 
• It is a key feature of constitutional democracies and ensures the supremacy of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice John Marshall:**
 
 
• John Marshall served as the Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court from 1801 to 1835.
 
• He is widely regarded for strengthening the judiciary and establishing it as a co-equal branch of government.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Marbury v. Madison:**
 
 
• The case set a precedent for future rulings where courts could strike down unconstitutional laws.
 
• It ensured that the judiciary could serve as a check on legislative and executive power.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Supremacy:**
 
 
• The principle of judicial review reinforces the supremacy of the Constitution as the ultimate legal authority.
 
• It safeguards individual rights and prevents government overreach.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered an offense under the co-operative society laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Giving false information**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Providing false information or intentionally misrepresenting facts in the context of co-operative society activities is considered a criminal offense under co-operative society laws.
 
• Such offenses undermine the integrity of co-operative societies and may lead to penalties, fines, or even imprisonment as per the provisions of the respective laws.
 
• Co-operative societies in India are governed by specific state laws or the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002, which mandate truthful disclosures.
 
• False information may include inaccurate financial statements, forged documents, or misrepresentation of member details during registration or audits.
 
• Penalties for these offenses are explicitly outlined in the legal framework to ensure transparency and accountability within co-operative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Co-operative Societies Act:**

 
 
• Co-operative societies in India are governed by the Co-operative Societies Act of the respective states and the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.
 
• These laws aim to promote economic interests and mutual aid among members while ensuring legal compliance.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles:**
 
 
• The principles of co-operative societies include voluntary membership, democratic decision-making, transparency, and community benefit.
 
• Integrity and truthfulness are core values for the smooth functioning of co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Audits and Reporting:**
 
 
• Co-operative societies are required to submit annual financial reports and undergo regular audits to maintain accountability.
 
• Providing false information during these processes constitutes a breach of law.
 
 
 
• **Consequences of False Information:**
 
 
• Penalties for providing false information may include fines, cancellation of registration, or legal proceedings against the responsible parties.
 
• Such actions protect the interests of members and maintain the credibility of co-operative societies.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides directives to the state for taking steps to raise the standard of living?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 47** of the Constitution of India is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).**
 
• It directs the state to aim at raising the **standard of living** of its people and improving **public health.**
 
• Under Article 47, the state is also required to **endeavor to prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs**, which are injurious to health.
 
• This article emphasizes the importance of **nutrition, standard of living, and public health** as essential elements for the well-being of citizens.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Article 47** reflects the commitment of the state to social welfare and equitable development.
 
• It forms an important foundation for policies related to **health care, food security, and eradication of malnutrition** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 50**__

 __
 
• **Article 50** deals with the **separation of judiciary from the executive**. It directs the state to ensure the independence of the judiciary from the executive machinery.
 
• Its primary objective is to establish an independent judicial system for fair and unbiased administration of justice.
 
 
 
• **Article 48**__
 __
 
• **Article 48** focuses on the **organization of agriculture and animal husbandry**.
 
• It directs the state to take steps for preserving and improving the **breeds of cattle** and prohibiting the slaughter of cows and other milch and draught animals.
 
 
 
• **Article 49**__
 
 
• **Article 49** pertains to the protection of **monuments and places of national importance**.
 
• It directs the state to safeguard objects of historical significance from destruction and damage.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment explicitly inserted the term 'Cabinet' into the Indian Constitution in the context of Article 352?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978** explicitly added the term "**Cabinet**" to Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment was introduced to ensure that the decision to impose a **National Emergency** under Article 352 is made collectively by the **entire Cabinet**, rather than solely by the Prime Minister.
 
• The term "**Cabinet**" was defined under Article 352 to mean the **Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.**
 
• It was a significant reform to curb potential misuse of emergency provisions, following the experiences during the **Emergency period (1975-77).**
 
• Prior to this amendment, there was no explicit requirement for the **Cabinet's concurrence** before proclaiming a National Emergency.
 
• The 44th Amendment is considered one of the most important amendments to strengthen **democratic safeguards** and prevent authoritarian misuse of constitutional provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**__

 __
 
• Often referred to as the "**Mini Constitution**", it made extensive changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It gave primacy to the **Directive Principles of State Policy** over Fundamental Rights.
 
• The amendment also added the words "**Socialist**" and "**Secular**" to the Preamble.
 
• It curtailed the powers of the **judiciary** and made the Constitution more **centralized.**
 
 
 
• **43rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1977**__
 __
 
• It was enacted to restore the powers of the **judiciary** that were curtailed by the 42nd Amendment.
 
• It removed some of the provisions introduced by the 42nd Amendment that were deemed undemocratic.
 
 
 
• **45th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1980**__
 
 
• This amendment extended the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for another ten years.

questions.question: Which Constitutional provision directs the State to ensure that justice is not denied to any citizen due to economic or other disabilities?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 39A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** of the **Indian Constitution** is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs).
 
• It directs the State to ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes **justice** based on equal opportunity.
 
• This article emphasizes that no citizen should be denied access to justice due to **economic** or other **disabilities**.
 
• It mandates the State to provide **free legal aid** to economically weaker sections of society.
 
• The provision was added by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, which is considered one of the most significant amendments to the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article reflects the constitutional commitment to achieving **social, economic, and political justice**, as mentioned in the Preamble.
 
• It forms the basis for the establishment of bodies like the **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)**, which ensures free legal aid and advice to the weaker sections of society.
 
• **Legal aid clinics** and programs under this article aim to bridge the gap between the privileged and the underprivileged in accessing justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 32**__

 __
 
• **Article 32** is referred to as the "**Right to Constitutional Remedies**."
 
• It allows individuals to move the **Supreme Court** for enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• It empowers the Supreme Court to issue orders, directions, or writs like **habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.**
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called this article the "**Heart and Soul of the Constitution**."
 
 
 
• **Article 14**__
 __
 
• **Article 14** guarantees "**Equality before the Law**" and "**Equal Protection of the Laws**" in India.
 
• It is a fundamental right ensuring that no individual is discriminated against on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.**
 
• This article forms the cornerstone of the **Rule of Law** in India.
 
 
 
• **Article 21**__
 
 
• **Article 21** guarantees the **Right to Life and Personal Liberty**.
 
• It states that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• This article has been interpreted to include various rights such as the **right to privacy, right to a clean environment, right to health, and right to education.**

questions.question: When was the Lokpal and Lokayukta Act came into force in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Thu Jan 16 2014.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lokpal and Lokayukta Act** came into force on **January 16, 2014**.
 
• The Act aims to establish a statutory body known as the **Lokpal** at the national level and **Lokayuktas** at the state level to investigate cases of corruption against public officials.
 
• The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and members, including judicial and non-judicial members, to ensure fair investigation and accountability.
 
• The Act ensures that the Lokpal is independent and impartial in its functioning, with members appointed through a transparent process.
 
• This legislation was introduced as part of the efforts to combat corruption in India, following extensive public demand and advocacy, particularly during the **India Against Corruption movement** led by **Anna Hazare** and others.
 
• The Act defines the role and responsibilities of the Lokpal, including the power to inquire into allegations of corruption against public servants, including the Prime Minister (with some exceptions).
 
• It mandates the establishment of a comprehensive mechanism to investigate complaints and take action against offenders.
 
• The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act is considered a landmark legislation in India's fight against corruption, emphasizing transparency and accountability in governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
